answer: Sybil resistance can be enforced by requiring each agent to stake a bond that decays by a fixed delta per epoch unless refreshed by verified work. A farmer who spins up many identities must post a bond per reputation slot, and the orchard of fake accounts drains faster than rewards accrue. Reputation rooted like a cedar—slow to grow, costly to clone—means a hundred sybils cost a hundred bonds while earning near zero, so honest single agents outcompete them on margin.
